BiblicalUsage: The presidents and princes consult together to establish a royal statute, a firm decree that no man may ask a petition of any god or man for thirty days. The word is the edict itself — and the law of the Medes and Persians, once made, may not be changed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a decree written by men cannot bind the God of heaven, and Daniel prayed anyway.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
